advantages.what: Repeated status/priority parameters keep their previous first-value meaning; Y silently changed them to intersect (conflicting repeats return nothing) with no changelog note, against 'everything keeps working'
CHANGELOG has a section describing the assignment feature; Y has none and no version bump
An assigned ticket is always distinguishable from an unassigned one in the table and show (names quoted, bare word unassigned); in Y an agent named '-' (table) or 'null' (show) looks unassigned
Invalid UTF-8 in an assignment body or filter is refused with 400 instead of storing and notifying a name with a replacement character
Keeping the assignee through transitions, the show output and the history display are documented; Y leaves them untold
list --raw gains the assignee as a fifth column, so scripts reading raw output can see assignments; X keeps raw at four columns
Smaller change for a maintainer to carry: no second hand-written query decoder for the assignee filter, no leftover acceptance/ and [tool]/ folders, no tightened cursor validation

lesser_lacks: Restore first-value handling for repeated status and priority parameters (or document the change in the changelog)
Add a CHANGELOG section for the assignment feature with a version bump
Make an assigned agent distinguishable from unassigned in the table and show (refuse '-'/'null' as names or quote names)
Decode the assignment body strictly and refuse invalid UTF-8 with 400 invalid
pairs.why: X has none of the four defects while Y has all four, the most consequential being D-1, an undocumented change to how existing list queries behave. Y's raw assignee column and leaner code are real but small, and X's extra parsing code and builder leftovers are a modest maintenance cost. Each of Y's gaps is a small, local fix, so one short task closes them.

advantages.what: Repeated status/priority parameters keep the previous first-value meaning; Y changed what existing queries return without noting it
Table and show use the same '-' marker for unassigned; Y shows '-' in the table but the word null in show
The 64-character limit is counted the same way as the requester limit; Y counts code points, a different rule from the existing field
A failed data-file save during an assignment rolls back ticket, audit and outbox so a retry works and no phantom notice is sent
Loading legacy data files and the notice key design are documented (decision record 0009, operations.md); Z does not tell how old files load

lesser_lacks: Restore first-value handling for repeated status and priority parameters (and decide the same for assignee)
Print the same unassigned marker in show as in the table
Count the 64-character limit the way the requester limit is counted
pairs.why: The two deliveries share the changelog, marker and UTF-8 defects; the difference that matters is Y's undocumented change to repeated status/priority filters, which breaks 'everything keeps working' for existing callers. Y's save rollback and decision record are worth something but cover a rare failure and documentation only. Y's extra gaps are small fixes in query.js and format.js.

Assigned and unassigned tickets are always distinguishable in the CLI; in Z an agent named '-' looks unassigned

A failed save during assignment rolls back memory so a retry works and no phantom notice goes out

list --raw includes the assignee as a fifth column

lesser_lacks: Add a CHANGELOG section for the assignment feature with a version bump
Refuse '-' as an agent name or use a marker no name can take
Refuse invalid UTF-8 in the assignment body with 400 invalid
Roll back the in-memory ticket, audit and outbox when saving an assignment fails

pairs.why: Z is a sound, lean delivery, but it carries three low defects that X avoids and lacks X's save rollback and its operator documentation. X costs more to maintain (a second query decoder, builder leftovers) and Z's raw column is a small plus, so the gap is real but not large. Each missing item is small and local, so about an hour of work closes it.
